risk.line: HIGH, held for an EIGHTEENTH consecutive pass, and today's movement is in the return address rather than on any front line. Riyadh's foreign ministry now says the drones that shut the East-West pipeline came from Iraq, and Saudi and American officials are pointing at Iranian-backed Iraqi militias rather than at the Houthis who were blamed first - which matters because Iraq is a file on which Washington already owns a strike playbook and Yemen is not. Underneath the attribution the physical numbers are the story: Saudi crude supply fell 2.3 million barrels a day in August to about 6 million, the lowest in more than three decades, Brent ran toward 105 dollars, and US diesel crossed 6 dollars a gallon for the first time on record. CRIT still requires an American killed or an American hull hit in the fighting now under way, and neither has happened in ten days.

forecasts.q: The Houthis or an entity they control publicly institute a MANDATORY transit requirement or any charge for Bab al-Mandab passage - a published rule, not a threat, not the existing voluntary scheme
forecasts.note: OPENED at 38, and the number is deliberately BELOW the tempting analogy. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing that licenses a design read at all: the Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center has published a voluntary, free 'Safe Transit Request' scheme since 2025 - 48 hours notice, ship name and passage details, an answer inside a day, non-sanctioned vessels only - and on 1 August the movement explicitly DENIED any plan to charge ships, citing the UNCLOS rule that bars levying fees for mere passage. Taking Mocha, Dhubab and Perim converts that paperwork into an office. The Sound Dues logic and Iran's own PGSA, stood up within about ten weeks of gaining strait leverage, both argue yes. It is held under 50 because the counter-incentives are specific and strong: the voluntary-and-free version already buys de facto sovereignty recognition at zero diplomatic cost, which is the movement's actual product; a fee would unite Cairo, whose Suez revenue depends on the same water, with the Gulf, and would invite the naval response Washington has so far declined to mount. If it comes, it will be priced as a SERVICE - escort, pilotage, inspection - not as a toll.

forecasts.q: Russian average monthly territorial gains in Q4 2026 fall below their Q2-Q3 2026 average (ISW/DeepState)
forecasts.note: 63, up five, and this is the biggest mover on the board. Michael Kofman's falsifiable claim - that Russian recruitment would stop covering casualties and offensive TEMPO would decline before any line broke - has until now been argued from casualty arithmetic. Today it has territory: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps cut the Russian salient between the Nitrius and Zherebets rivers north of Lyman and retook more than 200 square kilometres, eliminating the springboard Russia spent roughly eighteen months building toward Sloviansk and Izium. The detail that makes it credible is the sourcing order - Russian military bloggers reported the reversal before Kyiv confirmed it, and they had no incentive to invent it. Capped at plus five for two reasons: ISW states plainly that public evidence is insufficient to size the counterattacks, and the Pokrovsk axis is untouched. The seasonal base rate independently supports the direction - autumn rasputitsa and winter have historically depressed mechanised tempo against summer.

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly announces enrichment, weapons pursuit, or a nuclear-sharing arrangement
forecasts.note: 21, up three, on the cleanest print this model has had. Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma says a junior partner reads what its patron REFUSES, not what it promises; Scott Sagan's security model attaches the consequence - states build when the credibility of someone else's guarantee falls, not when the threat rises. Today both halves printed at once. The threat leg: both Saudi westward outlets closed inside thirty hours, with Petroline shut and Perim in Houthi hands. The guarantee leg: the crown prince asked the American president twice for strikes and was refused twice, receiving intelligence, targeting data, roughly 160 to 200 personnel and an Admiral Cooper visit instead. This stays at 21 rather than 35 because the question asks for an OVERT announcement and hedging is normally covert - the number is a deliberate floor on a trend it cannot fully see, and the observables are a fuel-cycle clause, a reactor tender or Pakistani personnel, not a speech.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, formal and holding more than 30 days
forecasts.note: 20, up two, and the smallness is the discipline. Three legs moved together for the first time since the talks froze: Zelenskyy told Deutsche Welle 'yes, of course' when asked whether he would meet Putin at the G20 the United States hosts at Trump National Doral on 14-15 December; American negotiators have shuttled between Kyiv and Moscow; and a Russian delegation confirmed attendance at the G20 energy meeting. It is only two points because willingness is the cheapest signal in diplomacy and it came from the side that wants the meeting - Putin has not reciprocated. The base rate governs the ceiling: 79 per cent of interstate wars end within two years, and this one is in its fifth, which is the part of the distribution where hazard rates DECLINE rather than rise. Long wars get longer. The falsifier is armed: Peskov restating the 'deep pause, no new proposals' line after a formal invitation kills the move.

forecasts.q: Major US and/or Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes (multi-day, state targets)
forecasts.note: 46, down two, and the cut is deliberately partial because this morning already spent two points on the same class of evidence and marking an echo is the error this desk has been caught making. The new facts are not echoes. Trump publicly attributed the pipeline attack to Iran - 'probably behind it' - and in the same set of remarks said the Houthis had asked the United States not to intervene, after refusing Riyadh twice. Revealed preference beats attribution every time: a president who will not strike the AGENT over a struck ally's pipeline is not about to reopen a multi-day campaign against state targets in the PRINCIPAL. An attribution the attributor will not act on is a declaratory move, not a predicate. The watch item that would reverse this is a Treasury designation naming the Iraqi group and its financial network - that is when words become an instrument.

forecasts.q: Front-month Brent settles at or above $120/bbl on any daily settle before 31 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: 49, down three, because the demand leg finally printed and it cuts against the barrier. The IEA's September report cuts 2026 world oil demand by 2.5 million barrels a day - 940,000 steeper than its August number and the largest annual contraction since the pandemic - with the losses concentrated in middle distillates and petrochemical feedstocks, and the rate of decline easing from 5.3 million in the second quarter to 2 million by the fourth. Supply falls further, by 5.7 million, with the Gulf recovery pushed to 2027, which is why this is a three-point cut rather than a rout. But the tape is the tell: Brent slipped below $105 on Friday, on the day Perim fell, up about nine per cent on the week and not squeezing. Stage discipline applies - a supply shock that meets demand destruction fizzles at Stage B, and the collapse ending is not the default ending.

33, up two: the political track slipped while the kinetic one did not. The US-mediated round scheduled for Rome this month has been pushed to October and downgraded to an ambassadors meeting at the State Department, and President Aoun said in Nabatieh there will be no new negotiations while Israeli operations continue. On the ground at least twenty-nine people have been killed in two weeks, Israel detonated a reported 1,100 tonnes of explosives inside the Ali al-Taher ridge on 11 September, and shelling hit al-Mansouri, Douha, Arnoun and Wadi al-Salouqi. Schelling's test caps the move at plus two: an operation that CONSOLIDATES a declared line is coercive bargaining, one that extends past it is a campaign, and both governments are still using the consolidation framing. Diplomacy receding is not the same thing as a campaign starting.

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to the US occurs in September 2026 roughly as planned
forecasts.note: 92, up two, and it is a routine outside-view raise rather than news. The visit is confirmed for 24 September at the White House, twelve days out, with no cancellation signal; Xi is travelling normally, and used the Delhi BRICS summit to call for the bloc to take a peacemaking role in the Gulf - which reads as pre-summit positioning, a leader arriving in Washington with something to sell, not a leader preparing to cancel. Announced head-of-state visits with active sherpa preparation are consummated more than ninety per cent of the time, and the residual shrinks as the date closes. This is the kind of move that should be boring; a forecast that only ever changes on drama is badly calibrated.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover to more than 50 per cent of pre-war volume (about 65 a day against a 130 baseline)
forecasts.note: HELD at 10 for a NINTH instance of the same pattern. Gulf foreign ministers meet Iran's Abbas Araghchi at Salalah on Monday, the fourth dated venue this desk has watched produce an announcement rather than a transit. What has changed is Tehran's hand rather than its intention: a party that has just watched a second chokepoint close without lifting a finger arrives at a safety meeting with more to trade and less reason to hurry. Watch the meeting for a named administrator, a fee schedule or an escort arrangement - a toll regime always announces itself as a safety mechanism.

forecasts.q: The US ULSD diesel crack spread settles below $45/bbl on any daily settle before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: HELD at 23 with the two new facts pointing opposite ways, which is the honest reason not to mark it. Against: Petroline's terminus at Yanbu also charges the Yasref and Yanbu refineries, roughly 650,000 barrels a day of distillate-heavy Europe-facing capacity, and a crude line that is not pumping cannot feed them. For: the IEA now expects the demand losses to fall most heavily on middle distillates, which is demand destruction in the exact barrel this question prices. Diesel at the American pump is a record $6.06 a gallon against $3.71 a year ago. When the supply and demand legs of a spread move the same way, the spread does not have to.

forecasts.q: The FOMC raises the fed funds target range at or before the 9-10 December 2026 meeting
forecasts.note: HELD at 72 for a third consecutive session, and the hold is a refusal to double-count rather than an absence of news. The energy shock got worse today and the board went RED for a fourth business day, but this question turns on a sentence rather than a barrel: whether the 16 September statement drops look-through on energy, as the ECB did last week. Marking an oil headline into a rate question before the committee has spoken is exactly the error the 6 September audit caught in this question's own history.

forecasts.q: USD/JPY appreciates 8 per cent or more from its 3 September level (160.0 to 147.2 or below) in any rolling 30-day window, before 31 Mar 2027
forecasts.note: HELD at 31 with a clean data vintage for a third session. The BOJ meets on 18 September and Takata is on record that the Bank should move nimbly - a hike into a strong dollar is the mechanism that turns a funding trade into a forced unwind, which is the whole reason this question exists. Nothing in today's energy shock touches the barrier arithmetic, and marking a yen question on an oil headline is the kind of cross-contamination this book is supposed to refuse.

forecasts.q: Saudi authorities publicly confirm a force majeure at Yanbu, Jizan or Ras Tanura, OR a reduction in East-West (Petroline) throughput, before 31 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: RESOLVED YES on 12 September - Brier 0.314, the worst score on this ledger against GEO-009's 0.029, mean 0.171 across two resolutions. Kept on the board rather than retired because the post-mortem is the point: the defect was in question DESIGN, not in the world. Joining two limbs with OR meant the easy limb - any throughput reduction - carried the question, and the Ministry of Energy's precautionary shutdown announcement satisfied it within a day of opening. A question that can be resolved by a press release is not a forecast.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Saudi Arabia blames Iran-backed Iraqi militias for pipeline attack
brief.h: Riyadh's foreign ministry said several drones 'coming from Iraq' hit the East-West pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions on Thursday morning, causing injuries and damage, and Saudi and US officials are now pointing at Iranian-backed Iraqi militias rather than at the Houthis who were blamed first.
brief.t: The important move today is not the attack, it is the return address. A Houthi strike on Petroline is a Yemen problem, answered with air defence and patience. A strike flown out of Iraq is a Baghdad problem, and Baghdad is a file on which Washington already owns a legal and operational rail - the militia-strike playbook built in 2019-20 against Kataib Hezbollah, up to and including the Soleimani precedent. Attribution is not commentary here; it is the act that decides which target set becomes available and which government gets the bill. And the bill lands on the weakest party in the room: Iraq gains nothing from this and stands to lose its own export licence, which is why the pressure now sits on Baghdad to police Maysan province before someone else does it for them.
brief.context: EPOCH: a late chapter of the 1973-74 bargain in which American protection was exchanged for dollar-priced oil - the pipeline exists only because that bargain was doubted after 2019. RAIL: Petroline runs roughly 1,200km from Abqaiq to Yanbu and has recently moved 4-5 million barrels a day, some 4-5 per cent of world supply, specifically so Gulf crude never has to clear Hormuz. DESK: the deciding desk is not the State Department podium but CENTCOM's targeting cell and OFAC's Iraq file - a designation naming an Iraqi group and its money is the cheap move, a strike is the expensive one. BASE RATE: after Abqaiq in September 2019, attribution took about ten days, the US named Iran, and no retaliatory strike followed. The modal outcome of a Gulf infrastructure attack is a sanctions listing plus an air-defence deployment, not ordnance. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: an American casualty on Saudi soil, which is the same threshold that turned the 2019-20 Iraq file kinetic.

angles.effect: Gains a named culprit it can take to Washington, but naming Iraq rather than Yemen is also an admission that its air defence failed against a threat axis it was not watching
Pays for a launch it did not order - the state that hosts the militia carries the export and banking risk, and has already moved against its own Maysan command to avoid becoming the target set
Keeps deniability because the launch point, the crews and the militia are Iraqi even where the supply chain is not, and collects the price effect without owning the act
Carry the transmission - diesel hit a record 6.06 dollars a gallon on Friday against 3.71 a year ago, and that is the number that reaches voters

dec.kill: A Treasury designation naming the specific Iraqi group and its financial network, or forensic recovery of airframes showing Iranian production, moves this from a ministry statement to evidence. Silence on both for two more weeks means the attribution was diplomatic rather than forensic.

consp.claim: That Saudi oil exports have already gone to zero and the figure is being suppressed, and separately that the pipeline is wrecked for six to twelve months - a /biz/ thread put the repair estimate at 'six months to twelve months' after running the satellite fire images through an AI model, and concluded 150 dollar oil is now locked in.
consp.spread: A 'SAUDI OIL EXPORTS DROPPED TO 0' thread on /pol/ ran past 160 replies, and matching '150 dollar oil' threads are running on /biz/ alongside a viral Jim Cramer post; the repair-duration figure circulates with no engineering source attached.
consp.read: Standard chokepoint maximalism, and it has a real kernel - Saudi crude supply did fall 2.3 million barrels a day in August to about 6 million, the lowest in over three decades. The leap is from a precautionary valve closure to a destroyed line: an AI-generated repair estimate built on fire-detection pixels is not an engineering assessment, and the Payne Institute's flaring analysis of the same nights points the other way.

brief.head: Riyadh weighs its Pakistan pact after Trump refuses air cover twice
brief.h: Mohammed bin Salman phoned Trump twice on Thursday asking for American strikes on the Houthis and was told Washington would not intervene directly for now but would share intelligence, leaving the untested Saudi-Pakistan-Turkiye mutual defence pact signed in Mecca as the kingdom's only other formal call option.
brief.t: Follow what was refused, not what was promised. The Mecca Pact was signed with Pakistan in September 2025 and widened to include Turkiye in August 2026, with a joint secretariat in Riyadh and Pakistan holding the first three-year chair - a NATO-shaped instrument under which the attacked member has to ask for a named kind of help rather than the clause firing automatically. That design is the tell: it was built as a hedge against exactly this week, an American no. But an alliance that has never been invoked is a price quote, not a guarantee, and invoking it carries a cost Riyadh may not want - it would put Pakistani or Turkish assets into a Yemeni war on the Saudi side and hand Tehran a much larger argument about who is escalating.
brief.context: CONSTRAINT before character: MbS is not choosing between friends, he is discovering the price of a guarantee. DESK: the decision sits with the Saudi defence ministry and the pact's Riyadh secretariat, and on the other side with Pakistan's Rawalpindi command, which has to weigh Gulf money against a Chinese and Iranian border file it cannot ignore. MECHANISM: Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma - a junior partner fears abandonment and entrapment at once and reads what its patron refuses, not what it says - with Scott Sagan's security model attaching the sequel, that proliferation follows a guarantee losing credibility. BASE RATE: Pakistan has been asked before. In 2015 its parliament voted unanimously to refuse Saudi requests for troops, ships and aircraft for the Yemen campaign and sent a token training contingent instead; the base rate for 'Gulf ally invokes and Islamabad deploys combat power' is close to zero. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a formal invocation letter, or Pakistani air-defence crews appearing at Saudi bases.

angles.effect: Buys a non-war before the midterms and keeps the 'no forever wars' line intact, while paying in alliance credibility that gets repriced by every other guarantee holder from Taipei to Warsaw

Receives intelligence and targeting data instead of ordnance - a security guarantee denominated in data - and every week it holds converts into a stronger domestic argument for an independent deterrent
Gains enormous leverage simply by being asked, and can bank that leverage without ever deploying; the pact is worth more to Pakistan untested than tested
Wins the week either way - Reuters reports the Houthis also phoned Washington asking it to stay out, which is what a party that is winning on the ground asks for

dec.kill: A formal Saudi invocation under the pact, or the arrival of Pakistani or Turkish combat aircraft or air-defence units in the kingdom, proves the instrument is real. Another month of Houthi strikes on Saudi cities with no invocation proves it is paper.

consp.claim: That the 'Islamic NATO' is a deliberate fiction and Pakistan has already quietly refused Riyadh - a /pol/ thread titled 'HAPPENING: PAKISTAN REJECTS SAUDI ARABIA' circulates alongside a longer 'Islamic NATO - what happened to this organization?' thread arguing Turkiye and Pakistan have gone silent on purpose since the Saudi oil facilities were hit. A parallel thread reads the Houthi breakthrough as a deliberate Washington-Riyadh betrayal of Yemeni government forces, quoting a senior Yemeni officer that 'the failure this time is not with the Yemenis, it's a disaster made in DC and Riyadh'.
consp.spread: Several /pol/ threads through 11-12 September, amplified by video of Houthi fighters filming a convoy of captured US-supplied vehicles.
consp.read: The 'alliance is fake' frame is doing real analytical work here because its kernel is checkable and largely true: the pact is untested, Pakistan's 2015 refusal is on the record, and no member has issued a statement of intent this week. The betrayal reading is weaker - abandonment and collusion look identical from the ground, and the simpler explanation is a patron declining a cost, not staging a defeat.

brief.head: AfD polls 37pc in Mecklenburg as Merz's CDU collapses to 7pc
brief.h: A Forschungsgruppe Wahlen survey for ZDF eight days before the 20 September state election puts the AfD on 37 per cent against the SPD's 34, with the chancellor's CDU on 7 - what would be the worst result any CDU has recorded in a German state election.
brief.t: The number that matters is not the 37, it is the 7. Germany's containment of the AfD has never been a wall, it is an arithmetic: as long as the other parties can assemble a majority without it, a plurality buys nothing. That arithmetic was load-bearing on the CDU being large enough to be part of every sum. At 7 per cent in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern the CDU stops being a coalition input in that state at all, which leaves an SPD-Linke government as the only anti-AfD arrangement available - a left coalition administering a state where the right-nationalist bloc is the largest single force. That is how a firewall survives an election and still loses legitimacy: it starts visibly requiring an unpopular coalition to work.
brief.context: RAIL: the Brandmauer is not a law, it is a set of party-congress resolutions binding coalition negotiators, so the deciding desk is the CDU federal executive and the SPD's state association, not the voters. BASE RATE: the AfD has done this once already - in Thuringia in September 2024 it took 32.8 per cent, the first far-right win of a German state election since the war, and was still excluded, with Mario Voigt's CDU governing alongside the BSW and SPD. The base rate for 'AfD leads a state poll and then governs' is nil. CLOCK: the vote is 20 September and further eastern and Berlin contests follow, so this is the first of a sequence rather than an isolated result. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: any CDU state association publicly accepting AfD votes to pass a budget - the firewall dies by toleration arithmetic long before it dies by coalition.

angles.effect: Wins the narrative either way - governing would be a prize, but exclusion after a plurality is the better fuel, and the party's whole organising story is that the system refuses to count its voters
Pays the entire bill; a 7 leaves him arguing that the eastern CDU is a rounding error while he holds the chancellorship on a coalition with the SPD
Holds a state it was expected to lose, at the price of governing with Die Linke and owning everything that goes wrong there for five years
Benefits without acting - a German coalition consumed by containment arithmetic is one that argues slowly about Ukraine funding, which is the return on every cheap information operation in the region

dec.kill: The poll is not the result. If the AfD lands below roughly 33 on 20 September, or the CDU recovers into double digits, the arithmetic story dissolves and this is an ordinary eastern protest vote.

consp.claim: That the German result is being managed - that media framing and institutional pressure exist to suppress the AfD vote, and that any outcome short of an AfD government proves the election is decorative. The same threads carry an ethnic-scapegoat narrative around European migration policy, assigning the policy to a named minority rather than to the governments and employers who set it.
consp.spread: Running on /pol/'s Europe-facing threads through the week and on X around the ZDF poll release.
consp.read: The containment claim has a checkable kernel and needs no conspiracy: the Brandmauer is public, written down and openly defended, so 'they will not let the AfD govern' is simply true and is not evidence of fraud. The scapegoat layer is the persuasion technique to name - agency transfer, moving responsibility from institutions that can be audited to a group that cannot set policy - and it is logged as a circulating narrative, not repeated.

brief.head: Court strikes down Trump's emergency order keeping a coal plant open
brief.h: A unanimous DC Circuit panel rejected the Energy Department's repeated orders forcing the 64-year-old JH Campbell plant in Michigan to run past its planned May 2025 retirement, after roughly 259 million dollars in costs had already accrued for ratepayers to absorb.
brief.t: Judge Cornelia Pillard's line is the whole ruling: the Federal Power Act's emergency provision is a 'narrow, last-resort backstop' for something immediate that states and utilities cannot handle themselves, not a tool for reversing a retirement planned years in advance. That is a limit on a specific technique - using a wartime-shaped statute to do industrial policy Congress has not voted for. Watch the timing, because the same administration is right now weighing the Defense Production Act of 1950 to add refining capacity, with diesel at a record 6.06 dollars a gallon and US refineries running near 98 per cent. One emergency rail just got narrowed while another is being loaded, and the court has published the standard the second one will be measured against.
brief.context: RAIL: section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act dates to 1935 and was written for storms and wartime - historically it is invoked for days or weeks, which is why courts rarely had to define its limits. This order ran far longer and generated a quantified bill, which gave Michigan's Dana Nessel and her Illinois and Minnesota counterparts a concrete injury to litigate. DESK: DOE's Office of Electricity issues the orders and FERC decides who pays, so the cost-allocation docket, not the press release, determines whether Midwestern ratepayers eat the 259 million. BASE RATE: emergency-powers rulings against an administration are more often narrowed than reversed on appeal, and the department is still pursuing similar orders at plants in Washington, Indiana, Colorado and Florida and at a Pennsylvania oil and gas facility. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: an en banc rehearing or a Supreme Court stay, or DOE simply reissuing on a narrower record.

angles.effect: Loses the instrument but keeps the constituency - the order was always worth more as a signal to coal-state voters than as megawatts, and a court blocking it supplies a grievance at no electoral cost
Carry the 259 million unless FERC allocates it elsewhere; 'keeping the lights on' was paid for by people who were never quoted the price
Gains either way - it is reimbursed for running a plant it had already written into retirement, and carries no litigation risk
Pays the real cost - a narrowed 202(c) standard is now precedent that will be cited against a Defense Production Act refining order before the ink dries

dec.kill: DOE reissuing a 202(c) order on a fuller record and surviving review, or a Supreme Court stay, would show the limit is rhetorical. Formal invocation of the Defense Production Act for refining inside the next month is the tell that the executive has simply switched rails.

consp.claim: That the diesel spike is engineered or deliberately allowed - threads tie record pump prices to Republican senators calling for emergency welfare payments to farmers and to Trump's promise of 5,000 dollar payments, and read the sequence as manufactured scarcity that justifies both the cheques and federal control of refining. A related line insists the US 'could take the Strait back in 24 hours if we really wanted to', so the shortage must be a choice.
consp.spread: Multiple /biz/ and /pol/ threads, including a record-diesel thread past 120 replies, plus a viral Kobeissi Letter post on X reading the 5,000 dollar promise as a 1.5 trillion dollar stimulus.
consp.read: The rescue-withheld frame, resting on accurate reporting: the White House did meet nearly a dozen refiners and is weighing the Defense Production Act, and diesel did cross 6 dollars. The design leap ignores the boring constraint - US refining has almost no slack left, and no statute builds a distillation column inside an election cycle.

brief.head: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 7,000 cases with no vaccine for the strain
brief.h: The epidemic detected in Ituri in mid-May has reached 7,022 cases and 3,398 deaths across seven provinces, with 837 people in isolation or treatment and the newest case in South-Ubangi on the borders of the Central African Republic and Congo-Brazzaville.
brief.t: The reason this one got away is a single technical fact that almost never makes a headline: it is the Bundibugyo virus, and the world's Ebola countermeasures are strain-specific. The licensed vaccine and the approved antibody treatments were all built against the Zaire strain, so the stockpile that ended the 2018-20 Kivu epidemic is, against this virus, a warehouse of the wrong thing. Everything the response has is therefore 1970s technology - trace contacts, isolate, bury safely - applied across seven provinces of a country where the state is thinnest exactly where the virus is moving. At 3,398 dead this is already double DR Congo's previous worst and the second-largest Ebola outbreak recorded anywhere, behind only West Africa in 2014-16, and it has run four months with barely a front page.
brief.context: MECHANISM: the global outbreak system runs on pre-positioned stockpiles - the International Coordinating Group allocates Ebola doses held against Zaire ebolavirus, and Bundibugyo has surfaced only a handful of times since 2007, so nobody stockpiled for it. That is not negligence, it is how insurance against rare events fails. DESK: the deciding desks are WHO AFRO and Africa CDC on declaration and case definition, Gavi and the ICG on doses, and the DRC health ministry on burial and contact-tracing teams - none of them a head of state, which is part of why the story carries no political clock. BASE RATE: DRC's previous largest outbreak, North Kivu and Ituri in 2018-20, reached 3,470 cases and 2,287 deaths over two years with a licensed vaccine available from the first weeks; this one passed that in four months without one. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: an emergency-use authorisation or trial deployment of a Bundibugyo-active candidate, or confirmed spread into the Central African Republic or Congo-Brazzaville, which converts a national emergency into a regional one.

watch: An Aramco October loading programme for Yanbu, at normal volumes or not at all. It is still the only document that separates a routing interruption from a production loss, and it outranks every ministry statement on either side.

A US Treasury designation naming the specific Iraqi militia and its money. That is the cheap move available to Washington, and its absence two weeks from now tells you the Iraq attribution was diplomatic rather than forensic.

A formal Saudi invocation of the Mecca Pact, or Pakistani or Turkish air-defence crews arriving in the kingdom. The pact has never been used, and an untested mutual defence clause is a price quote rather than a guarantee.

Whether the Defense Production Act is actually invoked for refining rather than merely weighed. Diesel at 6.06 dollars is the political clock, and a court has just published the standard that emergency-statute industrial policy will be measured against.

The 20 September vote in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern against the 37-34-7 poll. Watch the CDU number more closely than the AfD one - containment in Germany is coalition arithmetic, and it fails when the CDU is too small to be part of the sum.
lesson: Today's lesson is Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma, and it explains why a refused airstrike is a proliferation event. Snyder's insight, from 1984, is that every junior partner in an alliance fears two opposite things at once - ENTRAPMENT, being dragged into its patron's war, and ABANDONMENT, being left alone in its own - and that the two fears trade off, so everything a patron does to calm one inflames the other. The practical consequence is that clients learn far more from what a patron REFUSES than from what it promises, because refusals are paid for in credibility while promises are free. Scott Sagan's security model of proliferation attaches the consequence: states build nuclear weapons not when the threat rises but when the credibility of someone else's guarantee falls, which is why the historical cases cluster around abandonment moments rather than danger peaks - France and Britain after Suez in 1956, South Korea in the year the Nixon Doctrine withdrew a division. What that predicts right now is specific and checkable: Saudi Arabia asked Washington twice this week for strikes on the Houthis, was twice refused, and was handed intelligence and targeting data instead - precisely the substitution Sagan's model says a client notices and prices. The honest counter-case is that overt announcements are rare because hedging is normally covert, so the observable to watch is not a speech but an enrichment clause quietly dropped from a nuclear cooperation agreement, a reactor tender, or Pakistani personnel arriving under the Mecca pact - which is why our ledger's 21 per cent is deliberately a floor on a trend it cannot fully see.

quiz.q: Why does the loss of Perim island matter even if Saudi Arabia repairs the East-West pipeline quickly?
options: Because the pipeline physically runs through Perim
Because the pipeline's terminus at Yanbu ships out through Bab al-Mandab, which Perim now overlooks
Because Perim is where most Saudi crude is refined
Because insurers will not cover any pipeline within 500km of a war zone
quiz.why: The two facts are a chain, not a coincidence. Petroline exists to carry crude across the peninsula to Yanbu so it avoids Hormuz; Bab al-Mandab is how those Yanbu cargoes leave the Red Sea. Fixing the pipe without holding the gate just moves the bottleneck.

quiz.q: Our ledger raised the odds of a Saudi nuclear announcement this week. What drove the raise?
options: Iran was confirmed to have restarted enrichment
Saudi Arabia's oil revenue fell below its fiscal breakeven
Washington twice refused Riyadh's request for strikes and offered intelligence instead
Pakistan publicly offered to station warheads in the kingdom
quiz.why: Sagan's security model says states build when the credibility of someone else's guarantee falls, not when the threat rises. A patron that supplies targeting data instead of ordnance is the exact substitution a client prices - and Snyder's alliance dilemma says clients read refusals, not promises.

quiz.q: Brent slipped on Friday, the day Houthi forces completed their seizure of the strait's mouth. What is the best explanation?
options: Traders had not yet learned about the seizure
The IEA cut 2026 world oil demand by 2.5 million barrels a day, the largest contraction since the pandemic
Saudi Arabia released strategic reserves
OPEC raised production quotas that morning
quiz.why: A supply shock meeting demand destruction can leave price roughly where it was. This is why our board cut the odds of Brent reaching $120 rather than raising them - most energy-crisis stories fizzle at the second stage, and the honest model has to be able to say so.

quiz.q: Why did the Lyman counterattack move our Russian-tempo forecast, when earlier casualty estimates did not?
options: It was the first time ISW gave a confirmed figure
It converted an argument about manpower into observable terrain - an axis of advance was deleted
It proved Russia has run out of ammunition
It was reported by Ukraine's general staff rather than by analysts
quiz.why: Kofman's claim was that recruitment would stop covering casualties and offensive tempo would decay before any line broke. Until now that lived in arithmetic; a removed salient is terrain. Note that Russian milbloggers reported it first - a claim that costs its own side is worth more than one that flatters it.

quiz.q: A commentator writes: 'Iran closed the last route around Hormuz this week.' Which observable would most directly test that framing?
options: Whether Iranian officials praised the attacks
Whether Brent closed above $100
Whether the drones' launch province, operating group and airframe origin can each be separately identified
Whether the UN Security Council convened
quiz.why: The framing compresses three distinct actors - Iran, Iraqi militias in Maysan, and Ansar Allah in Yemen - into one hand. Baghdad's own investigation located the launch in Maysan and sacked the commander there. Who gains from the compression: the attributor, who gets to name a principal without striking anyone. Who pays: Iraq, which becomes a target set for someone else's war.

plumbing.epoch: E1, the 1973-79 rail on which oil was yoked to the dollar and Gulf surpluses were recycled into Treasuries, meeting E6, the 2019-21 plumbing-break-to-velocity-permit sequence still open in the form of an unended bill-buying programme. Today E1 was the one that moved, and a correction to yesterday's note belongs here: that security-for-barrels bargain is E1 in this module's numbering, not E4. Its unstated term was that the guarantor would keep the sea lanes open and would show up when a client was attacked. Both halves were tested inside thirty hours - the East-West pipeline shut, the Red Sea gate taken, and the guarantor declining a treaty partner's direct request for strikes twice while offering intelligence and targeting data instead. The old rail: a security guarantee underwritten by a navy with forward basing. The new permit: the guarantee is now explicitly partial - freedom of navigation for the lane, the land war behind it is the partner's problem - and the repricing that follows is denominated in hedging instruments rather than in barrels. DESIGN READ, gated and declined: no rail predates this. The refusal reads as drift and force-structure reality rather than as a plan to push Riyadh toward a hedge, and the incompetence alternative is straightforward - an administration that has said it will not start new wars discovering that its clients read that sentence as being about them.

sections.t: Saudi Arabia lost both of its roads around the Strait of Hormuz in thirty hours: drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline carrying four to five million barrels a day to Yanbu, and Houthi forces took Perim island at the mouth of Bab al-Mandab. Mohammed bin Salman asked Washington twice for strikes on the Houthis and was refused twice, receiving intelligence and targeting data instead.

The pipeline is not the story; the answer is. Since 1945 the bargain has been security for oil priced in dollars, on an unstated term: the guarantor defends the flow. Name the mechanism, the GUARANTEE LADDER - weapons, intelligence, escorts, and at the top, killing people who attack you. Clients assume they bought all of it; they bought only the rungs the guarantor's own interest will pay for. Riyadh reached for the top and was handed the third. Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma: a junior partner reads what its patron REFUSES more carefully than what it promises.

sections.h: Deep history I - when protection becomes tribute
sections.t: The oldest version of this ladder was built at Delos in 478 BC. The league was voluntary, aimed at Persia, and members could contribute ships or money. Most chose money, because money was convenient and crews were not. In 454 BC the treasury moved from Delos to Athens; phoros stopped meaning subscription and started meaning tribute, and some of it paid for the Parthenon. Thucydides records what became of members who tried to leave: Naxos around 470 and Thasos in 465 were besieged by the fleet they had helped finance. The guarantor prices the guarantee, and the price rises - but the sharper lesson is that the client's own convenience builds the cage. Those allies were disarmed by their preference for paying cash.

sections.h: Deep history II - real, and empty
sections.t: On 31 March 1939 Neville Chamberlain rose in the Commons and guaranteed Poland. It was formalised on 25 August as the Anglo-Polish Agreement of Mutual Assistance, carrying a secret protocol - published only after the war - that restricted the British obligation to aggression by Germany alone. So when the Red Army crossed on 17 September, Britain owed Poland precisely nothing. War was declared on 3 September; the French pushed a few miles into the Warndt forest and withdrew; Poland was finished in five weeks. The guarantee was legally genuine, publicly made and militarily undeliverable - honoured in declaration, void in relief, with the fine print written where the client could not read it.

sections.h: Deep history III - the hostage solution
sections.t: NATO was the attempt to fix that, and Article 5 repays reading slowly. Members assist by taking "such action as it deems necessary, including the use of armed force" - twelve lines where the Brussels Treaty's Article IV took four, because the US Senate would not sign automaticity. The famous clause is weaker than the clause it replaced. What made it hold for seventy-seven years was not text but Thomas Schelling's insight in Arms and Influence (1966): you cannot make a promise credible by asserting it, only by removing your own choice. American troops in West Germany and Korea, with their families, were no defence - at the Fulda Gap they would have been overrun in days. They were hostages, and a tripwire converts a future decision into an automatic consequence. Credibility bought with bodies, not adjectives. De Gaulle asked anyway - would Washington trade New York for Paris? - and answered himself with the force de frappe in 1960.

sections.h: Deep history IV - from the Quincy to Abqaiq
sections.t: On 14 February 1945, returning from Yalta, Roosevelt met Ibn Saud aboard the USS Quincy in the Great Bitter Lake. The ladder went up from there: the 1974 recycling arrangements; the Carter Doctrine of 23 January 1980, declaring an assault on the Gulf would be "repelled by any means necessary"; CENTCOM in 1983; half a million American soldiers deployed for a client state in 1991. The top rung was climbed exactly once. Then 14 September 2019: missiles and drones hit Abqaiq and Khurais and removed 5.7 million barrels a day, over half of Saudi production. The president said America was "locked and loaded," did nothing, and explained why in the sentence that has governed the Gulf ever since - that was an attack on Saudi Arabia, and it wasn't an attack on us. Seven years of Saudi behaviour follow: the Beijing-brokered normalisation with Tehran in 2023, and on 17 September 2025 the Saudi-Pakistan Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, signed with a nuclear-armed state and left deliberately vague on whether the arsenal is included. Pakistan's defence minister said the capability "will be made available," then walked it back. The ambiguity is not sloppiness. It is the French move, performed by a client who has learned how credibility gets manufactured.

Guarantees decay from the top down: you stop striking before you stop deploying, and stop deploying before you stop selling. The rung that survives serves the guarantor's own interest - Washington kept the lane open, an American problem, and declined the land war behind it. Clients rarely defect; they dilute. Where it breaks: in 1939 Britain wanted to help and could not, in 2026 America can and will not.

Mearsheimer holds that commitments bind only where the guarantor's own survival is engaged; everything else is cheap talk - the logic of his 1993 case for Ukraine keeping its warheads. Ikenberry holds that institutionalised orders outlive the power that built them. Mearsheimer takes WHICH rungs held: the US defended the commons it consumes, not the war it doesn't. Ikenberry takes why there was no rupture: Riyadh took the intelligence and stayed. Then Schelling against Mearsheimer on the remedy - Article 5 has held over Estonia, where no American survival interest exists, because American battalions stand on it. Schelling wins the mechanism, Mearsheimer the forecast that nobody will station a tripwire in Yemen. Sagan supplies the falsifiable consequence: states build when someone else's guarantee loses credibility, not when the threat rises.

The US produces some 13.8 million barrels a day, and near eighty per cent of Hormuz crude goes to Asia: American hulls escort Chinese and Indian barrels. That subsidy to a rival will not survive twenty years of fiscal stress in a country whose debt service exceeds its defence budget - Kennedy's overstretch, or more precisely Gilpin's rising protection costs. By 2035 the American Gulf posture converts from insurance into a fee-and-arms business: about 60 per cent. Bolder: at least one Gulf state holds an overt or thinly-veiled latent nuclear capability by 2035, about 55 per cent. Our twelve-month ledger line on a Saudi announcement is 21 per cent, and a floor: hedging is covert, so watch reactor tenders for a fuel-cycle clause. Counterweight: announced after Suez and after Saigon too. Disconfirmers: US strikes on the Houthis within sixty days, or a ratified treaty with Riyadh.

Glenn Snyder, Alliance Politics (1997) - the abandonment-entrapment dilemma. - Thomas Schelling, Arms and Influence (1966), ch. 2-3 - why a tripwire beats a treaty. - Scott Sagan, "Why Do States Build Nuclear Weapons?" (International Security, 1996).
